rules.title: Just Cause For Eviction Ordinance (JCO)
rules.requirement: Landlords may not terminate a tenancy without just cause, such as nonpayment of rent, an uncured lease violation, nuisance or damage, or illegal use. For no-fault evictions, such as owner or family move-in, demolition or removal from the rental market, the landlord must pay relocation assistance.
rules.coverage_text: Most residential properties in the City of Los Angeles that are not regulated by the Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO), including buildings newer than October 1, 1978 and properties with only one single-family dwelling. It applies to a tenancy once the tenant has lived in the unit at least six months or the original lease has expired, whichever comes first.
rules.exemptions: Transient hotels, licensed care facilities, fraternity or sorority houses, the owner's roommate, cooperatives under certain circumstances, some non-profit facilities for the homeless or short-term substance abuse treatment centers, and some properties owned by HACLA or the government.
rules.quoted_span: It prohibits terminations of tenancies without just cause and requires relocation assistance for no-fault evictions.
rules.interaction_text: The JCO covers most residential properties in the City of Los Angeles that are not regulated by the City’s Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO).

rules.title: Evictions for Non-Payment of Rent (Fair Market Rent threshold)
rules.requirement: Landlords may not evict a tenant who falls behind in rent unless the tenant owes more than the Fair Market Rent (FMR) for the unit's bedroom size.
rules.key_value: amount owed must exceed the Fair Market Rent (FMR) for the unit's bedroom size
rules.coverage_text: All RSO and JCO rental units in the City of Los Angeles.
rules.citation: Los Angeles Just Cause Ordinance (JCO) / Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO)
rules.quoted_span: Effective March 27, 2023, landlords may not evict a tenant who falls behind in rent unless the tenant owes an amount higher than the Fair Market Rent (FMR). The FMR depends on the bedroom size of the rental unit.

rules.title: Eviction Notices Filed with LAHD
rules.requirement: All eviction notices issued to tenants in the City of Los Angeles must be filed with LAHD within three (3) business days of service on the tenant.
rules.key_value: within three (3) business days of service
rules.coverage_text: All JCO and RSO rental properties in the City of Los Angeles.
rules.citation: Los Angeles Just Cause Ordinance (JCO) / Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO)
rules.quoted_span: Applies to all JCO & RSO rental properties – All eviction notices issued to tenants in the City of Los Angeles must be filed with LAHD within three (3) business days of service on the tenant.

rules.title: California Tenant Protection Act of 2019 (AB 1482) rent cap
rules.requirement: Annual rent increases are limited to no more than 5% plus the percentage change in the regional cost of living, or 10%, whichever is lower. From August 1, 2024 to July 31, 2025, the maximum allowable increase is 8.9%.
rules.key_value: 5% plus the percentage change in the cost of living for the region, or 10%, whichever is lower
rules.coverage_text: Buildings older than 15 years, on a rolling basis, that are not otherwise exempt.
rules.exemptions: Units constructed within the last 15 years (rolling basis); units deed- or regulatory-restricted as affordable to low or moderate-income households; certain dormitories; a two-unit property where an owner occupied the second unit for the entire tenancy; single-family homes and condominiums not owned by a real estate trust, corporation or LLC with a corporate member, where the landlord gave written notice of the exemption (this exemption does not apply if there is more than one dwelling unit on the lot or a second unit that cannot be sold separately); and units already subject to the City's RSO.
rules.citation: AB 1482, the California Tenant Protection Act of 2019 (Civil Code Section 1947.12)
rules.quoted_span: nual rent increases are limited to no more than 5% plus the percentage change in the cost of living for the region in which the property is located, or 10% whichever is lower
rules.interaction_text: -Units that are already subject to the City’s RSO.
